subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general `messages.messageRouting` or `internalWarningTarget` destination router for gateway lifecycle/internal warnings, or keep existing suppression plus subsystem-specific destinations as the supported model?
rationale: The user problem is source-backed, but solving it adds new config semantics and cross-channel delivery policy that should not be invented by an automated repair lane.

options.title: Design unified warning routing
options.body: Add an opt-in current-schema routing policy with explicit categories, default active-channel behavior, docs, and regression coverage across shared dispatch and affected subsystems.

options.title: Limit to suppression and subsystem knobs
options.body: Keep `messages.suppressToolErrors` and cron failure destinations as the supported model, and close or narrow broad routing requests accordingly.

options.title: Split by subsystem first
options.body: Handle tool errors, lifecycle notices, and cron notifications as separate smaller owner-boundary changes before committing to a unified config surface.

recommendation.title: Design unified warning routing
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in current-schema routing policy with explicit categories, default active-channel behavior, docs, and regression coverage across shared dispatch and affected subsystems.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the neighboring messages config surface and are the clearest history-backed owner for deciding whether that surface should grow.
